title: Permits for activities in forest reserves
rule: Activities inside national and local authority forest reserves need a permit under Part VI.
points: Felling or extracting timber for domestic sale, export, mining or prospecting.
Gathering forest produce, taking protected plant parts, building, running sawmills, roads, tourism, planting, hunting, fishing and grazing.
One permit can cover several activities.
Not every activity is allowed in every reserve.
A permit needs consistency with the management plan and compliance with other environment and land laws.
A permit does not remove the need for other licences.
Village councils may adopt Part VI by resolution for village land forest reserves and village forests. Domestic-use permits for villagers stay.
